holidays.name: Checkers Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the classic board game of checkers (draughts) by challenging a friend, a grandparent, or a stranger in the park to a showdown of diagonal jumping and king-making glory.
holidays.origin: Checkers Day is an unofficial observance, widely listed on September 23. It is also tied to the American political 'Checkers speech' that Richard Nixon gave on September 23, 1952, in which he mentioned his family's dog named Checkers.
holidays.funFact: Checkers is one of the oldest games in the world. Games resembling it have been traced back to ancient Mesopotamia around 3000 BCE, and in 2007 researchers announced the game had been 'solved,' meaning perfect play by both sides always ends in a draw.

holidays.name: Dogs in Politics Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek celebration of the time a cocker spaniel became the most famous pup in American politics. Observers honor the day by reflecting on how pets can sway public opinion, or by giving their own dog a very dignified treat.
holidays.origin: On September 23, 1952, vice-presidential candidate Richard Nixon delivered his televised 'Checkers speech' to defend himself against accusations of misusing campaign funds. He admitted he had accepted one gift: a black-and-white cocker spaniel named Checkers, and said he would keep it.
holidays.funFact: The speech was watched by an estimated 60 million Americans, one of the largest TV audiences of the era, and it saved Nixon's spot on the Eisenhower ticket.

holidays.name: Fall Equinox Celebration (Mabon)
holidays.description: A day when day and night are nearly equal in length, marked by harvest feasts, apple-picking, bonfires, and general autumn coziness. Modern pagans call it Mabon and celebrate balance, gratitude, and the second harvest.
holidays.origin: The autumnal equinox has been celebrated for thousands of years by agricultural societies. The name 'Mabon' was popularized in the 1970s by Wiccan writer Aidan Kelly, who borrowed it from a figure in Welsh mythology. The equinox often falls on September 22 or 23.
holidays.funFact: The popular belief that you can balance an egg on its end only at the equinox is a myth. You can balance an egg on any day of the year if you have enough patience and a steady hand.

holidays.name: Bi Visibility Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to celebrating bisexual people and raising awareness about biphobia and erasure, often marked with pink, purple, and blue flags, parties, and community events.
holidays.origin: Started in 1999 by activists Wendy Curry, Michael Page, and Gigi Raven Wilbur, who wanted to create a day for bisexual community recognition. It was first celebrated in the United States and has since spread globally.
holidays.funFact: The bisexual pride flag was designed by Michael Page in 1998, and its overlapping purple stripe was inspired by how blue and pink blend into purple, symbolizing how bisexual people exist in the overlap of two communities.

holidays.name: Great American Pot Roast Day... of Autumn: National Hojicha Tea Day... Just Kidding, It's International Day of Sign Languages
holidays.description: A genuinely meaningful observance in which people celebrate the richness of sign languages around the world, learning a few signs, and promoting deaf culture and linguistic rights.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly proclaimed September 23 as the International Day of Sign Languages in 2017, with the first observance in 2018. The date marks the founding of the World Federation of the Deaf in 1951.
holidays.funFact: There are over 300 different sign languages used around the world, and sign languages are not universal. American Sign Language is actually more closely related to French Sign Language than to British Sign Language.
